title.en: Lenz's law and conservation of energy

hook.en: Drop a strong magnet down a copper pipe and it falls slowly, as if through honey. The currents induced in the pipe push back against the falling magnet. That is *Lenz's* law at work.
hook.kn: ತಾಮ್ರದ ಕೊಳವೆಯೊಳಗೆ ಪ್ರಬಲ ಕಾಂತವನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟರೆ ಅದು ಜೇನಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಬೀಳುವಂತೆ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಬೀಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಕೊಳವೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರೇರಿತವಾದ ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳು ಕಾಂತವನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಇದೇ ಲೆನ್ಜ್ ನಿಯಮ.

body.en: The induced emf has a polarity such that the current it drives opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. If a north pole approaches a coil, the near face of the coil becomes a north pole and repels it. If the north pole moves away, the near face becomes a south pole and attracts it. The induced current opposes the change, not the flux itself.
body.kn: ಲೆನ್ಜ್ ನಿಯಮ: ಪ್ರೇರಿತ ಪ್ರವಾಹವು ತನ್ನನ್ನು ಉಂಟುಮಾಡಿದ ಅಭಿವಾಹ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಉತ್ತರ ಧ್ರುವ ಹತ್ತಿರ ಬಂದರೆ ಸುರುಳಿಯ ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಮುಖ ಉತ್ತರ ಧ್ರುವವಾಗಿ ವಿಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Lenz's law: the induced current always flows so as to oppose the change in flux that produces it. Bring a north pole towards a coil: the near face of the coil becomes a north pole and pushes the magnet back. Pull the north pole away: the near face becomes a south pole and pulls it back, so the current reverses. Either way you must do work against the magnetic force, and that work becomes the electrical energy in the coil. If the current helped the motion instead, energy would come from nothing. So the minus sign in Faraday's law is Lenz's law.

title.en: Lenz's law: the coil fights back

narration.en: The induced current always opposes the change that causes it. Push a N pole in and the near face of the coil becomes a N pole, pushing back. Pull it out and that face becomes S, pulling back. You must do work against this force, and that work becomes electrical energy.

caption.kn: ಪ್ರೇರಿತ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ತನ್ನನ್ನು ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುವ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. N ಧ್ರುವ ಒಳಗೆ ತಳ್ಳಿದರೆ ಸುರುಳಿಯ ಹತ್ತಿರದ ಮುಖ N ಆಗಿ ಹಿಂದೆ ತಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೊರಗೆ ಎಳೆದರೆ ಆ ಮುಖ S ಆಗಿ ಹಿಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಎಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಈ ಬಲದ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸವೇ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಶಕ್ತಿ.

say.en: The induced current always opposes the change that causes it. Push a N pole in and the near face of the coil becomes a N pole, pushing back. Pull it out and that face becomes S, pulling back. You must do work against this force, and that work becomes electrical energy.

body.en: If the induced current helped the change, a slight push on the magnet would make it speed up by itself, creating energy from nothing. Because the induced current opposes the motion, we must do work to move the magnet; that mechanical work appears as electrical energy and finally as heat in the coil. So *Lenz's* law follows from the conservation of energy.
body.kn: ಪ್ರೇರಿತ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗೆ ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದರೆ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಉಚಿತವಾಗಿ ಸಿಗುತ್ತಿತ್ತು. ವಿರೋಧ ಬಲದ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಮಾಡಿದ ಕೆಲಸವೇ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಶಕ್ತಿಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಲೆನ್ಜ್ ನಿಯಮ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆಯ ಪರಿಣಾಮ.

points.en: Opposition means work must be done

narration.en: If induced currents helped the change, we would get energy for free. Instead we must do work against the opposing force, and that work becomes electrical energy. So Lenz's law is conservation of energy.

problem.en: The north pole of a bar magnet is pushed towards a coil. In which direction does the induced current flow, as seen from the magnet's side?

steps.en: As the N pole approaches, the magnetic flux through the coil increases.
To oppose the approach, the near face must become a north pole.
A face looks like a north pole when the current in it appears anticlockwise.

answer.en: Anticlockwise, as seen from the magnet

As the N pole approaches, the magnetic flux through the coil increases.

A face looks like a north pole when the current in it appears anticlockwise.
So the answer is Anticlockwise, as seen from the magnet.

problem.en: A rectangular loop lies in the plane of the page in a field directed into the page. It is pulled out of the field region. Find the direction of the induced current.

steps.en: The into-page flux through the loop is decreasing.
The induced current must produce an into-page field inside the loop to make up for the loss.
By the right-hand rule, a clockwise current gives an into-page field inside.

By the right-hand rule, a clockwise current gives an into-page field inside.
So the answer is Clockwise.
